headline: High-risk shared cloud-workspace pair: Devin’s broad write/network/OAuth powers can leak, conflict, and cascade into Plane workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can read/write cloud workspace files, use MCP, and act autonomously; Plane exposes files, hyperlinks, notes, and issue/task content. A shared integration path could let attacker-controlled content from Plane be treated as instructions by Devin, but the pair lacks a documented direct parser bridge, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Devin ingests Plane notes, hyperlinks, or uploaded files as instructions without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF the two agents are connected through a shared MCP server or file handoff, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following from imported notes/files.
Require provenance labels on all Plane-to-Devin handoffs.
Use a read-only staging folder for shared artifacts.
Review MCP server allowlists before enabling shared access.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering at the integration boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin handles repo clones, cloud workspace files, and secrets such as deploy keys and integration tokens, while Plane touches files, notes, issues, and roadmaps. Devin’s broad network egress and Slack/GitHub/Jira/Notion writes create a realistic exfiltration path from shared work artifacts into external services, so the blast radius is sensitive and potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF sensitive repo or workspace files are present in the shared workflow, Devin can transmit them outward via its integrations.
IF Plane stores confidential notes or uploaded files in the same operational context, leakage can reach third-party services.
mitigations: Remove secrets from shared workspaces before pairing.
Restrict Devin’s outbound integrations to a test tenant.
Use separate principals for Plane and Devin.
Audit recent Slack/Jira/Notion writes for sensitive content.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP and egress allowlists on Devin’s integrations.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has filesystem write, git mutation, and broad shell/network powers; Plane is non-runnable here and has no write_filesystem permission, but it still manages mutable issues/tasks/files. The overlap is enough for conflicting updates to shared project state through integrations, though not the strongest same-directory write race.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same repo, issue, or roadmap item concurrently, last-write-wins conflicts can occur.
IF Plane is used as the coordination layer for Devin’s work, stale state can overwrite newer changes.
mitigations: Assign one agent as the sole writer per resource.
Use branch-per-agent workflows for git changes.
Freeze Plane edits during Devin runs.
Check for stale issue/roadmap timestamps before writes.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency controls across shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin can autonomously act on browser/shell/editor outputs, and Plane manages issues, tasks, and roadmaps that can become operational inputs. If Plane content is treated as authoritative by Devin, or Devin’s output is fed back into Plane without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect tasking or commits with real downstream impact.
conditions: IF Plane issues or notes are used as source-of-truth for Devin actions without human review, incorrect instructions can propagate.
IF Devin writes back summaries that Plane then reuses as authoritative, errors can amplify across workstreams.
mitigations: Require human approval before Devin acts on Plane-derived tasks.
Add a verification step for all Devin-generated summaries.
Limit Devin to draft-only updates in Plane.
Compare outputs against original tickets before execution.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware task routing and validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin is a closed-source cloud workspace agent handling source code, chat, and secrets, while Plane is open-source and self-hostable with files, issues, and notes. That creates a plausible residency/retention mismatch if Plane data is routed into Devin’s vendor-managed workspace, but the profiles do not document a specific regulated data class like PHI or EU PII, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Plane and then synced into Devin’s cloud workspace, residency or retention obligations may be violated.
IF the deployment requires self-hosted-only processing, Devin’s vendor-managed workspace becomes noncompliant.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared Plane items.
Use a self-hosted deployment for Plane when needed.
Route sensitive tickets to a separate workflow.
Review retention settings on Devin integrations.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention boundaries.
